chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Misma'i, from Isma'il ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):
He said: «Do not descend into the grave while wearing a turban, nor a cap, nor a ridāʾ, nor footwear; and unbutton your buttons.»

He (the narrator) said: I asked: «What about leather socks (khuff)?» He said: «There is no problem with leather socks at a time of necessity and taqiyya; and let him strive in that matter to the utmost of his ability.»

key_terms.تَقِيَّةٌ: taqiyya — religiously sanctioned dissimulation to avert harm

ai.seo_question: What items of clothing must be removed when descending into a grave according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the person who descends into the grave to place the deceased must remove the turban, cap, ridāʾ, and footwear, and unbutton their garment. An exception permits leather socks (khuff) in cases of necessity and taqiyya, yet even then one must exert every possible effort to observe the original ruling.
